panels.title: Server tick
panels.description: Server frame time, 5 s samples: the average and the longest single frame. The dedicated server runs at a fixed 30 fps, so 33 ms is normal; above it the server is falling behind the game clock, and a tall worst-frame spike is a save or a garbage-collection pause.

panels.title: Player ping
panels.description: Round-trip time to each player as Steam networking measures it. Above ~150 ms the player owning a zone makes its creatures stutter for everyone in it.

panels.title: Player throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second per player, one colour each: above zero is server → player, below zero is player → server.

panels.title: Day
panels.description: In-game day. Advances when everyone sleeps through the night.

panels.title: Last save took
panels.description: Duration of the latest world save. The world pauses while it writes.

panels.title: Peer timeouts
panels.description: Connections that stopped answering, total since tracking began.

panels.title: World objects
panels.description: Objects in the world right now: every placed item, creature, drop.

panels.title: World objects over time
panels.description: Networked object count over time, sampled every 5 s.

panels.title: Network packets / 10 min
panels.description: Packets to and from all players per 10 minutes, from Steam's per-connection packet rates.

panels.title: Worst frame
panels.description: Longest single frame in the last 5 s: a save or garbage-collection stall. The world stops for it.

panels.title: Creatures
panels.description: Creatures inside any connected player's active area, counted from the object store (a dedicated server instantiates none of them itself).

panels.title: Objects/s out
panels.description: Object updates the server sent to players in the last second.

panels.title: Weather
panels.description: The current environment as the game names it (Clear, Rain, ThunderStorm, Snow, Mist, …).

panels.title: Send queue
panels.description: Bytes waiting to be sent to each player. A queue that keeps growing means the player's link can't keep up with the world around them.

panels.title: Creatures by owner
panels.description: Who simulates the creatures near players: each creature is run by one player's PC (or the server, only around the world spawn). Vanilla gives them to whoever arrived first; a latency-aware networking mod moves them to the lowest-latency player who can see them.

panels.title: Raids and saves
panels.description: Straight from the game: a raid while one is running, a save while the world is writing, and in-game night. 5-second resolution.

panels.title: Send rounds/s
panels.description: How often the server ran a send round for each player. Vanilla serves one player per frame and starts a round every 50 ms, so the rate falls as players join; a per-tick send scheduler serves everyone every round. The dashed line is one round per server frame (30 fps), the most a 30 fps server can do.

panels.title: Starved rounds/s
panels.description: Rounds where the player got nothing because their in-flight window was full. Non-zero means the link (or the window size) is the limit, and that player sees the world in steps.

panels.title: Sync backlog
panels.description: Object updates waiting for each player at the start of a send round (peak per 5 s). Spikes on login and when walking into a base; a backlog that never drains is a player falling behind.

panels.title: Rounds carrying data
panels.description: Share of the player's send rounds that actually carried object updates. Low when the world around them is quiet, high in fights and busy bases.

panels.title: Packet loss
panels.description: Share of packets the player's client reports it did not receive, from Steam's connection quality. Loss, not ping, is what makes monsters rubber-band.

panels.title: Ownership handoffs / min
panels.description: Creatures near players that changed hands between players. A steady trickle is the mod moving simulation to the better-connected player; a constant stream would be thrashing.

panels.title: GC collections / min
panels.description: Managed garbage collections the server ran. Each one pauses the world briefly; tie a spike on Server tick to a collection here.

panels.title: Mod send scheduler
panels.description: NetworkPerformanceSystem's own counters: per-player sends completed per second, and rounds it cut short because its per-frame send budget (4 ms by default) ran out. Breaks mean the server is CPU-bound on sending.

panels.title: Objects/s out
panels.description: Object updates the server sent to all players per second.

panels.title: Player distance
panels.description: Distance between each pair of players. Below the dashed line they share an ownership area, which is when the networking mod's choice of who simulates a creature matters to both of them.
